servers.pinHint.title: Your Network group is getting long
servers.pinHint.body: Right-click a server and choose Unpin from switcher, or use “{command}” from the command palette. It stays in the Servers list.
servers.hub.status.waitingForKey: Waiting for you to check the key
servers.hub.editPickHint: Select a server to edit it.
servers.hub.editShareHint: A share has nothing to edit. To edit its server, select the server’s row.
servers.hub.editNearbyHint: {name} was found nearby and isn’t saved, so there’s nothing to edit.
servers.hub.openAccountHint: {name} isn’t a place to open. Open one of the buckets under it.
servers.hub.forgetAccountConfirm: Forget {name} and every bucket saved under it? Cmdr drops their connections and stops listing them. Your files stay in the buckets.
servers.hub.forgetSecretKeyToo: Also forget the account’s secret access key
servers.hub.forgetShareConfirm: Forget {name}? Cmdr stops listing it. If it’s mounted, it stays mounted, and your files stay on the server.
servers.hub.nearbyGroup: {count, plural, one {{countText} server found nearby} other {{countText} servers found nearby}}
servers.hub.nfsHint: NFS servers don’t announce themselves, so they don’t show up here.
servers.hub.emptyMessage: Add one below, or turn on a Mac or NAS on your network and Cmdr will find it.
servers.paneState.connectingHint: This can take a few seconds.
servers.refusal.needsCredentials: This server asks for a password.
servers.refusal.accountNotPermitted: {username} doesn’t have access here. Try a different account.
servers.refusal.authMethodUnsupported: This server uses a sign-in method Cmdr doesn’t support yet.
servers.refusal.certificateUntrusted: macOS doesn’t trust this server’s certificate. Add it in Keychain Access, then try again.
servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer: Nothing at this address answers WebDAV.
servers.refusal.invalidUrl: That doesn’t look like a server address.
servers.refusal.signInHelperStuck: {host} is answering, but macOS’s network sign-in helper looks stuck. To restart it, open Terminal, run killall NetAuthSysAgent, then try again. macOS starts the helper again on its own.
servers.refusal.localNetworkHint: If the server is on, check that Cmdr is allowed under {localNetwork}.
servers.refusal.certificateUnapproved: Cmdr hasn’t trusted the certificate for {host} yet.
servers.refusal.hostKeyUntrusted: Cmdr hasn’t trusted the key for {host} yet.
servers.refusal.hostKeyRevoked: The key for {host} is marked as compromised in your SSH settings on this Mac. Cmdr won’t connect to it.
servers.refusal.startFolderOutsideRoot: The start folder has to be the root folder or a folder inside it.
servers.refusal.rootNotFound: Cmdr can’t open this folder on {host}. Check that it exists and that your account can read it.
servers.refusal.startFolderNotFound: Cmdr can’t open this start folder on {host}. Check that it exists and that your account can read it.
servers.refusal.saveUnconfirmed: {host} didn’t answer in time, so nothing was saved. Try again in a moment.
servers.refusal.secretNotStored: Cmdr couldn’t store this password in your Keychain. Try again, or turn off “Remember in Keychain” to sign in without storing it.
servers.refusal.savedSecretNotUpdated: Cmdr saved your changes but couldn’t update the password in your Keychain. Save again to try once more.
servers.refusal.s3AuthenticationRejected: That secret access key didn’t work.
servers.refusal.s3NeedsCredentials: This account asks for a secret access key.
servers.refusal.s3SecretNotStored: Cmdr couldn’t store this secret access key in your Keychain. Try again, or turn off “Remember in Keychain” to sign in without storing it.
servers.refusal.s3SavedSecretNotUpdated: Cmdr saved your changes but couldn’t update the secret access key in your Keychain. Save again to try once more.
servers.refusal.accessDenied: This key can’t reach this bucket. Check the bucket name and the secret access key, and that the key may read the bucket.
servers.refusal.bucketListRefused: This key can’t list the buckets on this account. Type a bucket name to open that bucket, or check the secret access key.
servers.refusal.bucketNotFound: There’s no bucket by that name at {host}.
servers.refusal.regionMismatch: This bucket is in a different region. Pick its region and try again.
servers.refusal.regionMismatchNamed: This bucket is in {region}. Pick that region and try again.
servers.refusal.clockSkewed: This Mac’s clock is off by more than 15 minutes, so the server won’t accept Cmdr’s requests. Set the date and time automatically in System Settings, then try again.
servers.refusal.notAnS3Endpoint: Nothing at this address answers as S3 storage.
servers.refusal.exportNotFound: {host} has no export at that path. Pick one from the list, or check the spelling.
servers.refusal.exportRefused: {host} doesn’t let this Mac open that export. Check which computers the export allows in the server’s NFS settings.
servers.refusal.reservedPortRequired: {host} only accepts connections from a privileged port, which Cmdr can’t open here. Turn on the export’s “insecure” option on the server (some NAS apps call it “Allow connections from non-privileged ports”), then try again.
servers.refusal.noNfsV3: {host} doesn’t offer NFS version 3, the version Cmdr speaks.
servers.refusal.s3FieldMalformed: Use only a–z, 0–9, and dashes here.
servers.refusal.endpointMalformed: Enter the endpoint as http:// or https:// plus a host name, like https://s3.example.com.
servers.refusal.addressTaken: You already saved this address as {name}. Open that one instead, or forget it first to move this server here.
servers.refusal.secretNotMoved: Cmdr couldn’t take the saved password along to the new address, so nothing changed. Check that your Keychain is unlocked, then save again.
servers.refusal.s3SecretNotMoved: Cmdr couldn’t take the saved secret access key along to the new endpoint, so nothing changed. Check that your Keychain is unlocked, then save again.
servers.refusal.accountChanged: A different account is a different server, so nothing was saved. Add it as a new server instead.
servers.refusal.operationRunning: Cmdr is still working with files on this server, so nothing was saved. Let that finish or cancel it, then save the new address.
servers.refusal.shareMounted: The share {name} is still mounted from the old address. Eject it, then save again.
servers.refusal.shareEjectRefused: Cmdr couldn’t eject {name}, so nothing was saved. {reason}
servers.sheet.addAnywayHelp: Cmdr couldn’t check this server, so Add anyway saves it as you typed it.
servers.sheet.ejectAndSaveHelp: Cmdr ejects every share still mounted from the old address, then saves the new one.
servers.sheet.addedToast: {name} is saved in your Servers list.
servers.sheet.addressHelpSftp: A hostname, an address you copied, or a whole ssh line.
servers.sheet.addressHelpSmb: A hostname, an IP address, or an smb:// address you copied.
servers.sheet.addressHelpWebdav: A web address you copied, like https://nas.local/dav, or a hostname.
servers.sheet.addressHelpNfs: A hostname, or an address like nfs://nas.local/share or nas.local:/share.
servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeSmb: This looks like an SMB address. Pick SMB above if that’s what you meant.
servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeSftp: This looks like an SFTP address. Pick SFTP above if that’s what you meant.
servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeWebdav: This looks like a WebDAV address. Pick WebDAV above if that’s what you meant.
servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeNfs: This looks like an NFS address. Pick NFS above if that’s what you meant.
servers.sheet.webdavCleartext: This address isn’t encrypted, so anyone on your network can read the password Cmdr sends. Use an https address if your server has one.
servers.sheet.accountLocked: The protocol and the account are what name this server. To use another account, add it as a new server.
servers.sheet.identityLockedNfs: The server and the export are what name this place. To open another export, add it as a new server.
servers.sheet.nfsExportHelp: Pick one from the list, or type its path. A folder inside an export works too.
servers.sheet.nfsExportsNone: {host} lists no exports for this Mac. Type the export’s path if you know it.
servers.sheet.nfsExportsRefused: {host} doesn’t list its exports. Type the export’s path.
servers.sheet.nfsExportsUnreachable: Cmdr couldn’t reach {host} to list its exports. You can still type one.
servers.sheet.nfsIdentityHelp: The server decides what you can open by these numbers. NFS doesn’t ask for a password.
servers.sheet.nfsIdentityMostCommonOwner: Guessed from who owns the files in this export.
servers.sheet.nfsIdentityRootOwner: Guessed from who owns this export’s folder.
servers.sheet.nfsIdentityThisMac: Your IDs on this Mac. Change them if the files on the server belong to someone else.
servers.sheet.nfsUidZeroWarning: Most servers give user ID 0 no rights.
servers.sheet.nfsStartFolderHelp: Where the export opens. Leave it empty to open the export itself.
servers.sheet.s3EndpointMoveHelp: Did the server move? Type its new endpoint. Every bucket under this key comes along with its favorites and open tabs, and the saved secret access key comes too.
servers.sheet.addressMoveHelp: Did the server move? Type its new address. Its favorites, open tabs, and saved password come along.
servers.sheet.smbAddressMoveHelp: Did the server move? Type its new address. Its shares and saved password come along, and each share’s favorites and open tabs follow once that share opens at the new address.
servers.sheet.secretKeptPlaceholder: Saved in Keychain. Leave empty to keep it.
servers.sheet.smbUsernameHelp: Fill this in if your NAS needs an account. Cmdr asks for the password when you open a share.
servers.sheet.signInWithCredentials: Sign in with a username and password
servers.sheet.name: Name
servers.sheet.s3GcsKeyHelp: Sign in with an HMAC key from the Interoperability tab of your Cloud Storage settings.
servers.sheet.s3RegionOptionalPlaceholde: Optional. Leave empty to use us-east-1
servers.sheet.s3AccountIdHelp: The account ID on your Cloudflare R2 overview page.
servers.sheet.s3PathStyleHelp: Most self-hosted servers, like MinIO and Garage, need this.
servers.sheet.s3BucketHelp: Leave it empty to see every bucket. If your key is limited to one bucket, type its name.
servers.sheet.identityLockedS3: The provider, the access key ID, and the bucket are what name this place. Forget it and add it again to change them.
servers.sheet.identityLockedS3Account: The provider and the access key ID are what name this account. Forget it and add it again to change them.
servers.sheet.rootFolderHelp: Cmdr never goes above this folder on the server.
servers.sheet.startFolderHelp: Where the server opens. Leave it empty to open the root folder.
servers.sheet.autoReconnectHelp: If the connection drops, Cmdr reconnects to this server on its own. This doesn’t make Cmdr connect at startup: it connects when you open the server in a pane.
servers.sheet.needsStoredSecret: Reconnecting on its own needs a remembered password. Turn on “Remember in Keychain” and sign in once.
servers.hostKey.firstContactBody: Check the fingerprint below against the one the server’s owner gave you, then trust it.
servers.hostKey.changedBody: This can mean the server was reinstalled, or that something is sitting between you and it. Check the fingerprint with the server’s owner before trusting it.
servers.certificate.firstContactTitle: macOS doesn’t know the certificate for {host}
servers.certificate.firstContactBody: Home servers often make their own certificate. Check the fingerprint below against the one your server shows, then trust it.
servers.certificate.changedBody: This can mean the server got a new certificate, or that something is sitting between you and it. Check the fingerprint with the server’s owner before trusting it.
servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint: Its key changed. That can mean the server was reinstalled, or that something is sitting between you and it. Check the new key before you connect again.
servers.paneState.guestSessionRefused: Cmdr didn’t sign in to {name} as a guest
servers.paneState.guestSessionRefusedHin: You asked to sign in with your account, but the server offered a guest session instead. Usually that means the password was wrong. Rarely, it means someone is tampering with the connection.
servers.paneState.signedOutNothingToAsk: This server signs in with a key rather than a password, so there’s nothing to type. Open it again to retry.
servers.paneState.cancelCycleTooltip: Stop trying for now. The connection stays available. Switch back to retry.
servers.paneState.disconnectCycleTooltip: Stop trying and disconnect from the server.
servers.paneState.retryKeepsTrying: Will keep trying for a total of {duration}.
